title: Operating Lines of Credit Renewal Terms by Product
content:
Credit administration sets three renewal terms for each of the Operating Lines of Credit: how early a renewal request is accepted, how many renewals in a row may go through streamlined review, and whether current financial statements must come with the request.

## Terms

- **Renewal application window**: the calendar days before the maturity date from which a renewal request is accepted; 0 means the product is not renewable.
- **Streamlined renewals**: the consecutive renewals that may be approved under streamlined review before a full credit review is required.
- **Financial statements with renewal**: whether a current balance sheet and income statement must accompany a renewal request.

## Schedule

| Product | Renewal application window (calendar days before maturity) | Streamlined renewals in a row | Current balance sheet and income statement required |
|---|---|---|---|
| StartRight Operating Line | 120 | 2 | Yes |
| ExpressLine Operating Credit | 90 | 3 | No |
| Seasonal Operating Loan | 0 (not renewable) | 0 | No |
| Revolving Operating Line | 120 | 1 | Yes |
| Borrowing Base Operating Line | 150 | 0 | Yes |
| Agribusiness Revolving Line | 180 | 0 | Yes |

## Points of reading

- A streamlined allowance of 0 means every renewal of that product goes to full credit review; the Borrowing Base Operating Line and the Agribusiness Revolving Line are renewed only after full review.
- The ExpressLine Operating Credit is the only renewable product that does not ask for current financial statements with a renewal request.
- *Hypothetical illustration:* for a Revolving Operating Line maturing on 30 November, the 120-day window opens on 2 August of the same year.
